course.description:
本課程著重於環境微生物之基礎、生態與其在環境科學上的應用。微生物基礎部分包括細菌、真菌、藻類等微生物之分類、形態
和生理基本特性、培養、生長、代謝與控制等學理與操作技術等。而微生物生態則以其碳、氮循環與個別代謝的生化反應為基
礎，說明各類微生物於環境生態中所扮演的角色和重要性。同時說名類微生物之特殊生理代謝能力得於應用在能源工業、廢水和
廢棄物處理、生態環境復育，及農業等領域的學理依據與技術。

course.titleZh: 永續環境治理的設計思考
course.titleEn: Design Thinking for Sustainable Environmental Governance
course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
本課程以頭前溪流域為學習場域，結合永續發展目標（SDGs）、環境治理與設計思考方法，帶領學生從真實世界問題出發，探討
河川生態、水質污染、水資源治理、環境正義及地方文化等議題。課程透過課堂講授、實地走讀、專家座談、資料分析與團隊
專題等方式，培養學生跨域整合、問題分析、利害關係人溝通及社會實踐能力。學生將運用設計思考流程，發展兼顧環境、社
會與治理面向之創新方案，並藉由與在地社群、學校及公民團體互動，深化對流域治理與公共參與的理解，培養面對永續發展
挑戰所需之專業能力與社會責任。
course.objectives: Course keywords: 永續環境治理 Sustainable Environmental Governance,設計思考 Design Thinking,流域治理 Watershed Governance,水資源管理 Water Resource Management,社會實踐與公民參與 Social Practice and Civic Engagement      永續環境治理的設計思考Design Thinking for Sustainable Environmental Governance: Living in Harmony with the Hsinchu River一、課程說明（Course Description）頭前溪是孕育新竹地區發展的重要流域，也是新竹縣市民生用水、生態環境與產業發展的重要基礎。本課程以頭前溪流域為學習場域，結合永續發展目標（SDGs）、環境治理、設計思考（Design Thinking）及大學社會責任（USR）理念，引導學生從真實世界問題出發，探討河川生態、水質污染、水資源管理、環境正義、公民參與及地方文化等議題。課程透過課堂講授、跨域討論、專家座談、實地踏查、資料分析與團隊專題等方式，培養學生問題分析、利害關係人溝通、跨域整合及方案設計能力。學生將運用設計思考流程，從問題同理、需求探索、問題定義、方案發想、原型設計到成果驗證，提出兼顧環境、社會與治理面向之創新方案。本課程特別強調「從流域認識地方、從地方理解永續」，鼓勵學生走入頭前溪流域現場，透過與地方社群、學校、公民團體及政府部門互動，理解環境治理的複雜性與多元利害關係人觀點，培養未來面對永續發展挑戰所需之專業能力與社會責任感。---二、指定用書（Text Books）教師自編講義、案例教材及補充閱讀資料。---三、參考書籍（References）1. Brown, T. (2009). *Change by Design: How Design Thinking Creates New Alternatives for Business and Society.*2. United Nations. *Transforming Our World: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.*3. United Nations World Water Development Report.4. EPA (United States Environmental Protection Agency) Water Resources and Public Participation Resources.5. Climate Change Impacts on Freshwater Resources, EPA.6. Kernan, M., Battarbee, R., & Moss, B. (2010). *Climate Change Impacts on Freshwater Ecosystems.*7. 台灣河溪網（Taiwan River Network）8. 荒野保護協會（Society of Wilderness）9. 我們要喝乾淨水行動聯盟10. 頭前溪流域相關研究報告、政府公開資料及教師指定閱讀。---#四、教學方式（Teaching Methods）本課程採取「問題導向學習（PBL）」與「場域導向學習（Place-based Learning）」方式進行。教學方式包含：1. 課堂講授（Lectures）   * 永續發展、流域治理、水資源管理及設計思考相關理論。2. 分組討論（Group Discussion）   * 問題分析、需求探索及方案發想。3. 實地踏查（Field Study）   * 頭前溪流域、水環境場域及相關設施參訪。4. 專家座談（Guest Speakers）   * 邀請學界、政府、NGO及實務工作者分享經驗。5. 專題實作（Project-based Learning）   * 學生團隊提出永續環境治理方案。6. 成果展示（Presentation）   * 期中與期末成果發表與交流。---五、教學進度（Course Schedule）Week 1　課程介紹與頭前溪流域概論Week 2-3　實地走讀：舊港島、南寮及頭前溪出海口（9/19全天）Week 4　頭前溪流域地理、水文與歷史發展Week 5　河川生態、水質污染與環境風險Week 6　專家講座：河川廢棄物與公民科學Week 7　流域實地考察與現場觀察Week 8　頭前溪與新竹城市發展Week 9　期中成果報告Week 10　永續治理案例與利害關係人參與Week 11　公私協力與水環境巡守實務Week 12　關西鳳山溪走讀Week 13　竹東流域文化與地方走讀Week 14　垃圾處理與循環經濟場域參訪Week 15　水質大數據分析與治理應用Week 16　期末成果發表與方案展示---六、成績考核（Evaluation）課堂參與與出席　　　　　20%（含課堂討論、活動參與）團隊合作與平時作業　　　30%期中專題成果　　　　　　20%期末專題成果　　　　　　30%學生請假規定依《國立清華大學學生請假辦法》辦理。本課程包含多次實地踏查及場域學習活動，若因特殊原因無法參與校外教學活動，須依學校規定完成請假程序，並於事前通知授課教師。經核准請假者，應依教師指定方式完成替代學習作業，以維護學習權益。無故缺席校外活動者，將視同缺課並影響課堂參與成績。---七、生成式AI使用規範（AI Usage Policy）■ 有條件開放（Conditionally Open）本課程鼓勵學生善用生成式AI工具（如ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini等）作為學習輔助工具，例如資料蒐集、文獻摘要、構想發想、簡報整理及文本潤飾等。惟學生須遵守以下原則：1. AI不得取代學生之獨立思考與分析。2. 專題報告與作業須明確說明AI工具使用情形。3. 學生需自行查證AI產出內容之正確性。4. 實地觀察、田野調查、數據分析與個人反思不得完全由AI代為完成。5. 教師得要求學生說明作品形成過程及AI使用方式。未依規定揭露AI使用情形者，得視情況調整成績評定。---八、課程相關網站（Course-related Website）1. 聯合國永續發展目標（SDGs）   https://sdgs.un.org/goals2. 台灣河溪網   https://www.twrna.org3. 荒野保護協會   https://www.sow.org.tw4. 我們要喝乾淨水行動聯盟   https://www.facebook.com/hsinchu.drink5. 頭前溪流域行動平台（課程期間提供）

course.description:
本課程介紹質譜技術於環境分析之原理與應用，涵蓋液相與氣相層析串聯質譜（LC–MS/MS、GC–MS/MS）及感應耦合電漿質譜
（ICP–MS），並說明不同類型污染物之分析策略。課程強調環境污染物之檢測原理與應用，培養學生於環境監測與污染分析之基
本能力。
course.objectives: Course keywords: 環境質譜分析、新興污染物、層析分離技術、微量分析、環境監測 Environmental Mass Spectrometry、Emerging Contaminants、Chromatographic Separation、Trace Analysis、Environmental Monitoring      一、課程說明(Course Description)本課程旨在建立學生對質譜技術於環境分析中之核心概念與應用能力，內容涵蓋層析分離（液相與氣相液相）與質譜分析之整合，並結合LC–MS/MS、GC–MS/MS及ICP–MS等主流分析平台。課程將說明不同污染物之分析方法與儀器選擇原則，並介紹樣品前處理、定量分析、品質控制及數據判讀等關鍵技術。此外，亦將涵蓋新興污染物分析、非目標篩選及轉化產物鑑定等進階主題，修課學生將具備跨領域之環境分析能力，並能將質譜技術應用於實際研究問題。二、指定用書(Text Books)“Introduction to MassSpectrometry” J.T. Watson and O.D.Sparkman, 4th Edition, Wiley.“Mass Spectrometry-Principles andApplications” Edmond de Hoffmannand Vincent Stroobant, 3rd Edition,Wiley三、參考書籍(References)四、教學方式(Teaching Method)Lecture五、教學進度(Syllabus)LC–MS/MS、GC–MS/MS、ICP–MS六、成績考核(Evaluation)1.Midterm: 40%2.Final exam: 40%3.Report: 20%七、可連結之網頁位址

course.description:
This course introduces students to the core concepts and methods of statistics, with a
focus on learning how to use data effectively in the face of uncertainty. Key topics
include data visualization, descriptive statistics, probability, statistical inference, and
linear regression. Emphasis will be placed on building intuition and practical
understanding rather than mathematical rigor.
Students will develop the skills to make sense of data, draw meaningful conclusions,
and communicate results with clarity and confidence. The tools and thinking
developed in this course are valuable for making informed decisions and conducting
research across a wide range of disciplines. They also form the foundation of many
modern applications, including machine learning and artificial intelligence.

值。

course.description:
金融科技(Financial Technology, FinTech)是目前全球金融業與科技業的焦點，它所引發的破壞式創新，正挑戰既有金融
服務的供給方式和消費行為。本課程由資工、數學教授群共同開設，旨在釐清 FinTech 本質、相關的創新科技、以及關鍵的趨
勢。
同時我們也會在課程當中邀請相關學者專家進行演講，並在金融機構（或金融科技新創公司）的協助之下完成期末的AI程式競
賽。歡迎想參與或是有志於跨金融與科技領域的同學們，來共同一窺金融科技殿堂之美。

course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
In this course, Physical AI serves as the central lens through which all projects and discussions
are contextualized. Students will explore how modern AI models are integrated into real-world
systems such as robots, smart homes, and autonomous vehicles, and how intelligence,
embodiment, and environment jointly shape system behavior.
As AI systems increasingly operate around us in everyday life, critical questions emerge: How
do these systems function in real-world settings? How do we ensure their reliability, safety, and
alignment with human values? And what new challenges arise when AI is deployed in open,
dynamic environments?
If these questions inspire you, this course is designed for you.

course.description:
自二十世紀初現代考古學從西方傳入中國，這門學問便很快地在歷史悠久、族群及文化多元的中國土地上生根成長，至今已取
得了大量的研究資料和豐富的研究成果，不只對促進中國古代人類文化和歷史研究及文明進程的新理解有重要的貢獻，即使對
其它人文、社會科學，甚而自然科學領域的一些研究課題，例如:中國古代的社會型態、經濟變遷、工藝美術、科技發展、宗
教禮制、民族發展、族群遺傳、農業起源和天文星象等，也提供了非常珍貴的出土資料與證據。有些考古發現甚而成為令人嚮
往的世界文化遺產。因此，過去半個多世紀以來的這段時間，考古學在中國成為一門顯學，被稱為是中國考古學的黃金時代。
	本課程的目的是要介紹中國考古學的發展、發現，以及重要的研究成果和所探討的重要課題，期使選課的同學對中
國考古學有所認識和瞭解，並培養研究的視野、興趣和發展的能力。

course.description:
This seminar examines the relationships between the indigenous peoples and the  
state in Taiwan through historical periods, situating it in the settler colonial contexts.  
Historical reflection on the changing relationship between the indigenous peoples  
and the state equipped students to explain the contemporary dilemma faced by the 
indigenous people worldwide. With the concept of transitional justice emerging in  
Taiwan and elsewhere, this seminar will draw on materials and experiences in other  
Fourth World to compare with those of Taiwan’s indigenous peoples and seek to  
advance a better path forward.

course.description:
在日常生活中，許多時候情緒與倫理幾乎無法分開，而這份交纏並不止於私人生活，在現代制度之中同樣運作。本課程便從這份交纏出發，
借助人類學中兩個重要卻長期平行發展的理論傳統來理解它：倫理轉向（ethical turn）與情緒人類學（anthropology of 
emotions）。前者問的是人們如何在日常生活中成為倫理主體，後者則把情緒當作一個可以被田野觀察與描述的問題，去看人們如何在語
言、身體與人際關係之中感受、命名並賦予情緒意義。情緒的養成與倫理主體的形成，何以在許多時候難以分開，正是這門課想要一路追問
的問題。

course.description:
本課程將引導學生系統性認識考古學中石器研究的核心理論與分析方法，透過討論與案例分析，理解石器在重建人類行為與社會組織中的關
鍵角色。石器作為考古遺存中最常見且保存良好的材料之一，不僅提供了理解史前技術與日常實踐的證據，更是連結環境、經濟與文化行為
的重要媒介。課程內容涵蓋石器的類型特徵、原料選擇與取得策略、製作技術與操作序列、分類原則等基礎，以及技術組織理論、功能研
究、實驗考古學、民族考古學、過程與後過程等分析取徑，也討論如何從石器探討生計活動、勞動分工、資源利用與貿易交換等議題。透過
系統性的理論學習、案例研讀與實作訓練，學生將建立石器辨識、記錄與分析的基礎能力，也理解石器技術與使用策略所反映的人群行為與
文化意義，並能將相關分析方法應用於實際研究。

course.description:
This course is an undergraduate-level introduction to physical cosmology: the application of 
basic physics concepts to study the origin and evolution of the Universe. The emphasis will be on the 
"big picture" of how we learn about the structure and evolution of the universe from astronomical 
observations.
course.objectives: Course keywords: Cosmology, Astronomy, Astrophysics, Cosmological Observations, Galaxy Formation      課程說明 (Course Description)This course is an undergraduate-level introduction to the principles of cosmology: the study of the origin and evolution of the universe based on fundamental physics. The emphasis will be on astronomical observations, rather than particle physics. We will not use any mathematics more difficult than basic calculus. Although we will discuss concepts related to General Relativity, we will not do any GR calculations or derivations. The same is true for particle physics/quantum mechanics. There are no hard prerequisites for the course. However, you are expected to have a sound grasp of fundamental undergraduate physics at the 2nd-year level or above. You should understand the fundamental concepts of Newtonian gravity, special relativity and electromagnetic radiation (i.e. electron energy levels, the absorption and emission of photons) at the level of undergraduate "General Physics". Previous courses in basic astronomy will be extremely helpful.The course will be taught entirely in English, but you will be assessed on your understanding of the physical concepts, not your English ability. There will be a Mandarin-speaking TA.教學進度 (Syllabus)By the end of the course you should be able to:- Describe the principles of how distances to astronomical objects (like galaxies) are determined;- Describe the fundamental observational evidence for the expansion of the universe;- Understand the theoretical connection between the expansion of the universe and its contents;- Work with simple mathematic models of the expansion and understand how those models can be tested by observations;- Explain the origin and importance of the cosmic microwave background;- Describe the processes thought to have occurred in the first few minutes of the Universe, including "nucleosynthesis";- Explain the concepts of dark matter, dark energy and cosmic inflation;- Tell the (qualitative) story of how cosmic structures like stars and galaxies formed;- Appreciate some important open questions in modern cosmology.This course can be considered as a primer for the graduate course in cosmology offered by the Institute of Astronomy. This undergraduate course will not cover the practical, quantitative  mathematical framework needed to describe the formation and evolution of  structure, and to match cosmological observations to models. Frontier topics in cosmology will be covered only in a descriptive way, without calculations. 成績考核 (Evaluation)The exact evaluation method may be adapted depending on the class size, but will involve several homework assignments and a final exam.AI Policy: "有條件開放"Summary: AI use is acceptable as a supplement to learning, but answers to assessments must be your own work, and will be marked down for clear and uncritical use of AI tools. Use of AI in written assessments is discouraged and any such use must be clearly declared. Expect to be challenged to explain and prove your understanding if you hand in work suspected of being generated by AI without critical thought.Details: Using generative AI to help with your study is at least not worse than asking your classmates or reading random websites. There is no problem  with talking to your classmates (or AI) about the lectures or homework  assignments. You should not just accept what you are told, but always do your best to "absorb" and double-check any information on your own, and make sure you have a good "grip" on the ideas. Once you've learned about something from an AI chatbot, you should at  least try getting it to ask you some questions to test your understanding.This course involves some written assessment. Your answers to assessment  questions should *always* be your own, because the whole point of assessment is is to demonstrate to the instructor what *you* understand. Your answers to assessment questions should not come from your classmates, so they should not come from AI either. Some students use AI to "help with English". This course is not an English test, so there is absolutely no need to do that. The official language of the course is "broken English".  Your own honest answer in poor English is much better than someone else's answer in perfectly written English.教學方式 (Teaching Method)The course will be taught in a classical way, with weekly in-person lectures and recommendations for self-study. Basic lecture notes will be provided, but you are expected to read one or more textbooks by yourself.參考書籍 (References)The primary textbook for the course will be:- Introduction to Cosmology, by Barbara Ryden, 2nd Edition (Cambridge University Press, 2016) https://doi.org/10.1017/9781316651087As a second (easier but less complete) textbook, I recommend:- An Introduction to Modern Cosmology, by Andrew Liddle (3rd/revised edition, Wiley, 2015)You may also consider:- A Course in Cosmology, from Theory to Practice, by Dragan Huterer, 1st Edition (Cambridge University Press, 2023) https://doi.org/10.1017/9781009070232This is basically a slightly more advanced and up-to-date version of Ryden.More references will be given at the start of the course.

course.description:
This course is a graduate-level introduction to theories and observations of galaxy formation and 
evolution, in the concordance Dark Energy and Cold Dark Matter (LambdaCDM) cosmogony. It is a core 
course of the Institute for Astronomy graduate syllabus.
course.objectives: Course keywords: Astronomy, Astrophysics, Galaxy Observations, Galaxy Formation, Galaxy Evolution      課程說明 (Course Description)This course is a graduate-level introduction to the nature of galaxies -- what they are, where they come from, and how they change over time. These are major topics in astronomical research, building on knowledge from other areas such as cosmology and stellar astrophysics.The course is intended as a primer for graduate research. We will aim to cover a broad range of topics, rather than a rigorous mathematical treatment.PLEASE NOTE: The level will be suitable for graduate and senior undergraduate students whose major is Physics or Astrophysics. The course will assume an undergraduate background knowledge of astronomy.The course will be offered and assessed in English.The homework exercises will involve simple numerical equation-solving and graph-plotting tasks. Basic instruction in python will be provided.Students who have not previously taken a course in cosmology may find it helpful to follow the undergraduate "Introduction to Modern Cosmology" given by the same lecturer, although we will not consider more than the "big picture" of cosmology in this course.教學進度(Syllabus)The minimum syllabus is:1. Astronomical measurements and observational techniques2. Stars and stellar populations3. Describing the different types of galaxies4. The cosmological context of galaxy formation5. Galaxy "environments"6. Dark matter halo origins and structure7. The origin of galaxies, gas cooling8. Cold gas disks and star formation9. "Feedback" and chemical enrichment10. Gravitational dynamics11. Galaxy interactions and mergers12. Galaxy evolution over cosmic time13. Supermassive black holes14. Open problems in galaxy formation This course will be deliberately "simple" in assuming almost no prior knowledge.For the first time, there will be a second course in the Spring semester covering more advanced topics and details required for modern galaxy evolution research. Effectively they will be "part 1" and "part 2" of the same syllabus. The "part 2" advanced course will assume familiarity with all the topics covered here.教學方式 (Teaching Method)Lectures, reading assignments.成績考核 (Evaluation)Approximately 4 homework exercises and final quiz-style exam.指定用書 (Text Books)The reference textbook for this course will be:* "Dynamics and Astrophysics of Galaxies" by Jo Bovy (Princeton U. Press, 2026)https://galaxiesbook.org/We will not go through everything in this book, and we will not follow the chapters in the order they are presented (we will focus mostly on chapter 18).We will also make use of the classic textbook:* “An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics” (2nd ed.) by B. W. Carroll & D. A. Ostlie (2006, Pearson Addison-Wesley)Some alternative/additional textbooks about galaxies:* (Simple) Fundamentals of Galaxy Dynamics, Formation and Evolution by Ignacio Ferreras (2019, UCL Press). Free e-book: https://www.uclpress.co.uk/products/84078* (Advanced) “Galaxy Formation and Evolution” by H. Mo, S. White & F. van den Bosch(2010, Cambridge University Press)* (Advanced) “Galactic Astronomy” (2nd ed.) by J. Binney & M. Merrifield (2008, Princeton  University Press)For the cosmological background to the course, the following textbooks may be helpful:* “Introduction to Cosmology” (2nd Ed.) by Barbara Ryden (2016, Cambridge University Press)* “An Introduction to Modern Cosmology” (3rd Ed.) by Andrew Liddle  (2015, Wiley)

course.description:
This course provides a structured forum for graduate students to present their research, develop 
professional-level scientific presentation skills, and become familiar with the breadth of ongoing 
research within the institute, fostering scientific discussion and potential collaboration.
course.objectives: Course keywords: Astronomy, Seminar, Presentation Skills, Professional Development      課程說明 (Course Description)Modern astronomical research is increasingly collaborative and interdisciplinary, spanning theory, observation, instrumentation, data science, and numerical simulation. Graduate students must not only develop deep expertise in their own research area, but also acquire the ability to communicate their work clearly to diverse audiences and engage constructively with work outside their immediate specialization.  This seminar course provides a structured environment in which students present their ongoing research to peers, postdoctoral researchers, and faculty, receive constructive feedback on scientific communication, and learn about current projects across the institute. The format emphasizes work-in-progress presentations, discussion, and methodological exchange, thereby strengthening the intellectual cohesion of the graduate program and supporting the professional development of students as researchers.  The course will:●	Develop effective oral scientific communication skills ●	Provide regular opportunities for students to present their own research ●	Expose students to the full range of research topics pursued within the institute ●	Foster critical scientific discussion and interaction ●	Encourage interdisciplinary thinking and collaboration among students and postdocsFormat: The first lecture would cover introduction to the seminar, expectations, and effective scientific presentations. Each of the remaining lectures would be composed of two presentations given by students as well as invited speakers (postdocs or faculties). Each presentation is 20-25 minutes plus 5-10 minutes for questions and discussions. Each presentation will be evaluated by the peers, the TA, and the instructor. The students are encouraged to ask questions to receive participation points.  The class is a required graduate research seminar for all astronomy MSc and PhD students (two semesters required for MSc students and four semesters for PhD students). It will be offered every semester. The course is one credit – one hour per week.成績考核 (Evaluation)Grades for this course will be evaluated based on:1. Participation (20%) Detailed instructions and report template are available on the eLearn system.相關網頁 (Website)1. However, in the field of astronomy alone, nearly 40 new papers are published every day. It is a significant amount of work to keep up with this flood of papers. The purpose of this course is to train students to efficiently read and understand the essence of new research papers within a limited amount of time. Students will spend no more than one hour reading a paper of their choice and will then take turns presenting a short  summary in 10 minutes. The focus will be on understanding the main points rather than getting into the details. It is not necessary to read every single detail of the paper. Additionally, other students in the class will have a valuable opportunity to learn about the latest papers while listening to the speaker. After each presentation, the instructor will teach a relevant physics concept related to the reviewed paper.The course will take place every Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday from 12:10 pm to 1 pm. During each session, three papers will be reviewed. Therefore, over the course of one semester, we will review almost 100 papers. By the end of the semester, students will be familiar with the latest advancements in astronomy.Previous knowledge is not required. We will focus on learning key concepts of astronomy as they arise in research papers. This bottom-up approach reflects the practical and realistic nature of everyday research life. The course will be conducted in English.Use of AI : Unrestricted use with no disclosure required-參考書籍 (References)Papers to be presented are selected from the following archive servers.https://www.benty-fields.com/http://arxiv.org/list/astro-ph/new-教學方式(Teaching Method)Presentations by students followed by a review by the instructor.-成績考核(Evaluation)Presentations.-Classroom Etiquette:To create a focused learning environment, please silence your cell phones during class sessions and exams.-Presentation Policy:If you are unable to attend your scheduled presentation date, please find someone to replace well in advance. Failure to do so will result in a reduction of your score.Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI):You are allowed to utilize AI tools for research and the preparation of your presentations.X-Class Format:This course is designed for flexible learning. All lectures will be recorded and made available online for your review. However, presentations must be given in person. course.description:
Molecular Simulation and Modeling (MD I) is the first half of a year-long sequence that introduces the 
theoretical foundations of molecular simulations. The course focuses on helping students understand 
key concepts behind molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of biomolecules. Topics include statistical 
mechanics and several widely used ideas and methods in molecular simulations.
Although modern software makes simulations easy to perform, correctly interpreting and troubleshooting 
simulations still requires understanding the basic principles on which these methods are built. This 
course therefore explains these principles clearly and systematically.
course.objectives: Course keywords: molecular simulation, molecular dynamics simulation, statistical mechanics, numerical methods, optimization, sampling methods, free energy, 分子模擬, 分子動力學模擬, 統計力學, 數值方法, 最適化, 取樣方法, 自由能      ● 課程說明(Course Description)Molecular Simulation and Modeling (MD I) introduces the theoretical foundations of molecular simulations, with a primary focus on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of biomolecules. The course covers essential concepts such as statistical mechanics, energy minimization, integrators, constraints, and temperature and pressure control. These topics form the basis for understanding how molecular simulations are constructed, how they evolve in time, and how their results should be interpreted.Although modern software makes running simulations straightforward, correctly analyzing and troubleshooting them still requires a clear understanding of the underlying principles. This course therefore explains these principles in a systematic and accessible manner, emphasizing the reasoning behind commonly used simulation techniques.By the end of this course, students will be able to:Understand the statistical-mechanical principles underlying molecular dynamics simulationsExplain the role of energy minimization, integrators, and constraints in MDDescribe how temperature and pressure control are implemented and interpreted● 指定用書(Text Books)Lecture notes will be provided in class.● 參考書籍(References)1.	Benoît Roux. “Computational Modeling and Simulations of Biomolecular Systems.” World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd.2.	Michael P. Allen, Dominic J. Daan Frenkel, Berend Smit “Understanding Molecular Simulation: From Algorithms to Applications” (Computational Science Series, Vol 1).● 教學方式(Teaching Method)Lectures (theory-based instruction).● 教學進度(Syllabus)This course is part of a year-long sequence on the theoretical foundations of molecular simulations. The actual order and depth of topics may vary each year depending on the pace and background of the class. MD I introduces the fundamental concepts, and MD II continues with topics that build upon this background. As the class prioritizes student comprehension, the content is subject to change over the duration of the course.[MD I] 1.	Introduction to molecular simulations (MD & MC)2.	Equilibrium statistical mechanics3.	Energy minimization4.	Integrators5.	Constraints6.	Temperature control7.	Pressure control[MD II] (Topics covered in the second semester, for reference)1.	Brief review of MD I (focusing on key concepts)2.	Force fields3.	Long-range interactions4.	Coarse-grained models5.	Free energy methods6.	Enhanced sampling techniques7.	Additional topics as appropriate● 成績考核(Evaluation)Report (50%) Participation, including in-class questions and discussion (50%)● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)● Course policy for AI usagehttps://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248378.php?Lang=zh-twThis course adopts the following policy:R26; Conditionally open – Students must briefly disclose how generative AI was used (e.g., for topic ideation, sentence refinement, or structural reference) in a footnote on the title page or after the reference section of their assignments or reports.R26; If AI usage is discovered without proper disclosure, instructors or relevant units (including this course) reserve the right to reevaluate the assignment or withhold scores.

course.titleZh: 生醫工程光學與顯微影像分析
course.titleEn: Biomedical Engineering Optics and Microscopic Imaging Analysis
course.requirement: 醫工所115D 選修 醫工所115M 選修
course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
本課程介紹生醫工程光學與顯微影像分析之核心概念，涵蓋光學成像原理、顯微鏡系統架構、螢光與多模態影像技術，以及影像處理與分
析方法。課程結合理論講授、文獻討論與應用，培養學生掌握生醫影像擷取、定量分析與結果判讀能力，並進一步連結疾病診斷、細胞觀
察與醫學研究等實際應用，建立跨領域研究與創新發展基礎。
This course introduces the core concepts of biomedical engineering optics and microscopic image 
analysis, covering optical imaging principles, microscope system architecture, fluorescence and 
multimodal imaging techniques, and image processing and analysis methods. Combining theoretical 
lectures, literature discussions, and applications, the course cultivates students' abilities in 
biomedical image acquisition, quantitative analysis, and result interpretation. It further connects 
to practical applications such as disease diagnosis, cell observation, and medical research, 
establishing a foundation for interdisciplinary research and innovative development.

course.titleZh: 柔性生醫光電感測及技術應用
course.titleEn: Flexible Biomedical Optoelectronic Sensing and Technology Applications (AI with BioMEMS sensors)
course.requirement: 醫工所115D 選修 醫工所115M 選修
course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
本課程介紹柔性生醫光電感測之核心原理、材料、元件製作與系統整合，涵蓋柔性基板、光電感測機制、BioMEMS微製程、可
穿戴與即時
監測技術，以及AI輔助訊號分析與判讀。課程將結合理論講授、文獻討論與應用案例，培養學生掌握生醫感測器設計、資料
處理與臨床轉
譯能力，並能進一步發想智慧醫療、健康監測與精準診斷之創新解決方案。
This course introduces the core principles, materials, component fabrication, and system integration 
of flexible biomedical optoelectronic sensing. It covers flexible substrates, optoelectronic sensing 
mechanisms, BioMEMS microfabrication, wearable and real-time monitoring technologies, and AI-
assisted signal analysis and interpretation. The course combines theoretical lectures, literature 
discussions, and application case studies to cultivate students' skills in biomedical sensor design, 
data processing, and clinical translation, and to further develop innovative solutions for smart 
healthcare, health monitoring, and precision diagnosis.

course.description:
This course introduces soft materials from an engineering perspective, emphasizing how to design, 
process, characterize, and apply polymers, hydrogels, colloids, emulsions, and other soft systems in 
biomedical, manufacturing, and electronic applications.
Learning goals
1.	identify major classes of soft materials and where they are used
2.	connect material composition and processing to performance
3.	interpret common characterization data such as rheology, swelling, and mechanical tests
4.	choose suitable soft materials for a practical engineering problem
5.	analyze case studies in biomaterials, coatings, printing, and soft devices

This course is designed for first- and second-year BMES bachelor students, aiming to develop 
technical English skills specific to the discipline of Biomedical Engineering. The course will focus 
on improving students’ abilities in listening, reading, writing, and speaking. By the end of the 
course, each student will be expected to give an oral presentation, demonstrating their ability to 
organize content, utilize graphics and visual aids, and present information in a clear and logical 
manner.
course.objectives: Course keywords: English for Specific Purposes, English for Academic Purposes, Biomedical Engineering English, Technical English      一、課程說明(Course Description) This course is designed for first- and second-year BMES bachelor's students and aims to develop technical English skills relevant to the field of Biomedical Engineering while strengthening students’ engagement with the international academic community. The course will focus on enhancing students’ listening, reading, writing, and speaking abilities through content drawn from engineering, science, and medical science, helping them build familiarity with technical terminology.In addition to technical language development, the course will introduce and explore important contemporary issues in biomedical engineering, including gender inequality in clinical practice, research, and the workplace; ethical considerations in clinical trials and preclinical animal studies; and the social and environmental responsibilities associated with engineering and healthcare innovation.By the end of the course, each student will be expected to deliver an oral presentation that demonstrates their ability to organize content effectively, make appropriate use of graphics and visual aids, and communicate information in a clear, logical, and professional manner.二、教學方式(Teaching Method) Various topics within the field of Biomedical Engineering will be introduced. Technical information will be delivered through lectures, reading materials (text), and multimedia videos (listening). Each week, a list of relevant vocabulary will be provided. Throughout the semester, in-class exercises will facilitate practice through pair conversations (speaking practice), group discussions, written exercises, and opportunities for presentations.三、教學進度(Syllabus) R26; Intro to Biomedical EngineeringR26; BiomechanicsR26; Medical ImagingR26; Medical Devices and developmentsR26; Biomaterials and Tissue EngineeringR26; NanotechnologyR26; Computational systems biologyR26; Genetic EngineeringR26; Academic Writing (Reports, Journal articles, Thesis): structure and styleR26; Academic Presentations skills (Oral, Posters): effective methods and medium utilization四、成績考核(Evaluation)  - 60% class attendance and participation - 20% in-class exercises - 20% 5-min presentation

course.description:
生醫電子與儀器實驗是一為培養學生進入醫學工程領域所設計的跨領域應用課程。課程設計上，含跨基本電子元件儀器介紹及操
作、影像處理分析、自動控制程式與電訊號量測、基礎光學、微波與電磁波量測實驗。課程設計以生醫儀器所需的基本能力為主
軸，期透過實驗課程，以動手實做的上課過程，讓學生實地整合基礎科學知識，進而能啟發其創新能力。
course.objectives: Course keywords: 電子實驗(Electronics Experiments), 影像處理(Imaging Processing), 程式設計(Programming), 光學實驗(Optics Experiment), 光電實驗 (Photo-electric Experiment)      Course keywords:基本電子元件儀器，影像處理分，電訊號量測，基礎光學，微波與電磁波量測課程說明：1. 選課：考量儀器可用數量，每班上限25人，兩班皆滿額時才可加簽。2. 分組：由授課教師將每班分為四組(週一：ABCD，週二：EFGH)。3. 評分方式：各實驗負責老師針對所負責的實驗評分。期末成績以各老師之授課時間權重後相加平均。4. 出席：遲到10分鐘內扣該實驗成績的20%，超過10分鐘該實驗成績零分。未到者該實驗零分。若有由正當程序請假，實驗負責老師認可後，可找各實驗助教補做實驗。5. 報告繳交：統一於實驗下一次上課時繳交，課堂開始時收齊，遲交以零分計算。若上課老師不同，請各老師協助移交報告。教學進度(Syllabus)基本電子元件儀器介紹及操作影像處理LabviewBasic biosensing experimentElectromagnetic fields measurement experimentBasic optics experiment

course.description:
本課程旨在介紹生物化學之基本原理與生命分子之結構、功能及其相互作用，建立學生對生命現象分子基礎的理解。課程內容涵蓋水與生物
系統之熱力學、胺基酸與蛋白質結構、醣類、脂質、生物膜與膜運輸，以及核酸與酵素等重要主題。透過系統性講授與案例說明，使學生了
解生物大分子的化學特性與生理功能，並奠定後續分子生物學、生物技術、生醫工程及生命科學相關課程之基礎知識。

course.description:
This course is to provide the students who lack basic training in materials 
science an introduction to the fundamental concepts of biomaterials, including 
three types of biomaterials (metals, ceramics and synthetic and natural 
macromolecules) and their chemical structure, physical properties, processing and 
applications. Biocompatibility of materials pertinent to their applications in 
biomedical engineering is the other important issue to be given in this course. 
This includes the interactions of biomaterials with proteins and cells and 
biomaterial-elicited specific immune responses.

course.description:
1) 瞭解臨床醫學基本觀念及其相關疾病的表徵和治療重點
2) 內科、外科、急診、急救、婦產科、兒科等相關科學的基本介紹
3) 瞭解相關醫學術語、一般醫學知識、及臨床評估之意義
4) 瞭解並落實生醫科技領域當中基礎與臨床之結合
course.objectives: Course keywords: 臨床醫學(clinical medicine)，醫學知識(medical knowledge)，生醫科技(biomedical technology)，創新臨床醫療(medical innovation)，轉譯醫學(translational medicine)      課程說明  介紹臨床醫學的基本觀念，討論和其相關的議題，瞭解各科疾病，諸如:內科、外科、婦產科、小兒科、急救等之臨床表徵及其治療上的重點，當今治療面臨的問題，並學習與日常生活習習相關的醫療知識，最後展望未來醫學發展，推展生醫科技領域當中基礎與臨床之結合。  將專業艱澀的醫學知識，由受過醫環系教育的醫師整理介紹給醫環系或相關科系學生，藉以了解醫環系的研究如何在臨床醫學中找到相對應的研究題目。或是藉由課程的修習，能增加醫學常識，促進自己及周遭親朋好友的健康。指定用書(Text Books)：臨床醫學概論 華杏出版社 作者：洪敏元教學進度上課日期：1. 9/9, 16, 23, 30   10/7, 14, 21, 28   11/4, 18, 25   12/2, 9, 163. 停課：   11/11: 全校運動大會(停課一天)   12/23: 期末考週4. 課程內容： 心臟科：主動脈剝離、 心肌梗塞、心律不整、高血壓、心導管 眼科：近視雷射、視網膜剝離、兒童視力矯正、結膜炎、青光眼 腸胃科：胃痛、吐血、肝硬化、胃潰瘍、胃癌、幽門螺旋桿菌、B型肝炎 放射：Ｘ光、電腦斷層、磁振造影、超音波、血管攝影 外科：手術基礎技巧教學、 牙科：齲齒（蛀牙）、植牙、齒列矯正、牙周病、智齒阻生 一般外科: 肝癌、胃癌、乳癌、胰臟癌、急性膽囊炎、腹股溝疝氣、急性闌尾炎 婦產科: 子宮出血、月經異常、經痛、骨盆器官脫垂、安全期、巧克力囊腫、懷孕、自然產、剖腹產 急診科: CPR 、傷口處置、AED 教學、胸腹部外傷急症、燒燙傷、中毒 皮膚科：美容醫學、鳳凰電波拉皮、肉毒桿菌、黑頭粉刺、青春痘 大腸直腸外科: 痔瘡、血便、大腸癌、大腸鏡、糞便篩檢、達文西手術、肛門痛 小兒科: 新生兒、早產兒、兒童發展遲緩、異位性皮膚炎、尿布疹、輪狀病毒感染、疫苗 整形外科： 形體美容、重建本課程無涉及AI使用 Not applicable成績考核１．出席＋隨堂考：85％,  ２．期末報告：5 ％,  ３．課堂抽問：10%

course.prerequisites: 排除大學部1年級2年級3年級
course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
本課程探討人工智慧在醫學影像分析中的理論基礎與實務應用，涵蓋影像前處理、深度學習模型建構（CNN、Transformer）、
分類、偵測、分割任務等內容。學生將實作 DICOM 影像處理，學習使用 Python 進行醫學影像分析，並認識臨床應用與法規
挑戰。課程強調跨領域整合與團隊合作，適合醫學、工程、生物資訊等背景學生修習。

course.titleZh: 穿戴式生醫電子裝置設計
course.titleEn: Design of Wearable Biomedical Electronic Device
course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
With the internet of things (IoT) rapid development and advanced devices that can monitor a myriad 
of 
biometric parameters, wearable biomedical device has gained the interest of physicians and 
researchers due to the benefits that could be associated with long-term monitoring of patients for 
healthcare. The course will provide students with introduction to wearable biomedical devices and 
its principle is based on the latest academic research and commercial biomedical product 
development. 

The course will  guide students to see the overview of the current wearable biomedical devices and 
help them to train  their scientific thinking from initial unmet needs to device design, and further 
fabrication technologies for wearable biomedical devices.
course.objectives: Course keywords: 可穿戴感測器、電子感測器、非侵入式量測、非接觸式感測、磁場刺激      一、課程說明(Course Description) The course will provide students with an introduction to wearable biomedical devices and their principles. The content includes abundant multidisciplinary technologies, including circuit and system-level design, physics, electromagnetism, semiconductor process, micro/nanotechnology, etc. The recent academic research and commercial biomedical products will be presented and guide students to see the overview of the current wearable biomedical devices. The main goal of this course is to help students thoroughly understand wearable biomedical device products from initial unmet needs to design and eventually fabrication technologies.二、教學方式(Teaching Method) Lectures and presentations.三、教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Introduction to wearable biomedical device development2. Cardiac electrophysiology and ECG device 3. Hemodynamics and blood pressure device4. Photoplethysmography device5. Capacitive sensor, piezoelectric sensor, magneto-plethysmographic sensor, and force-sensitive sensor6. Electromyography device7. Electroencephalography device8. Bio-impedance sensors (impedance plethysmography, electrical impedance spectroscopy, and electrical impedance tomography)9. Capacitive coupling sensor10. Transcranial magnetic stimulation11. Self-power sensors四、成績考核(Evaluation) Class experiment (30%)Final presentation (70%)

course.titleZh: 核磁共振影像原理及應用
course.titleEn: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Principles and Applications
course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
This course introduces the fundamental concepts and applications of magnetic resonance imaging.  
The concepts include spin behavior, NMR signals, hardware, pulse sequence, and k-space. The technical 
applications regarding fast scan, parallel imaging, and artifacts will be covered in this course. We 
will also introduce some of the clinical applications, e.g., fMRI, angiography, diffusion, and 
perfusion.

course.titleZh: 超音波與光學：生醫技術與應用
course.titleEn: Ultrasound and Optics : Biomedical Imaging Techniques and applications
course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
The course will cover three biomedical imaging techniques: Ultrasound, Optical, and Optoacoustics. 
Fundamentals physics, signal detection, and image formation for each modality will be discussed, 
followed by their applications. An emphasis will be placed on the contrasting and complementary 
nature between the first two: ultrasound and optical methods. This will lead the discussion into the 
third topic of photoacoustic techniques and applications, where the characteristics, highlights, and 
current limitations will be explored. In the last portion of this course, students will have a 
chance to exercise logical reasoning and creative problem solving skill in anticipating and 
resolving potential problems
course.objectives: Course keywords: Medical diagnostics, Biological Imaging, Ultrasound imaging, Optical technique, Photoacoustic/ Optoacoustic imaging, Image processing，醫療診斷, 生物影像，超音波成像，光學技術，光聲成像，影像處理      一、課程說明(Course Description)The course will start with a revision on the motivations of biomedical imaging, along with common techniques and challenges. Then, we will zoom in on ultrasound imaging techniques: from acoustic wave propagation in tissue to the understanding of transducers and image formation. As we explore system designs and their applications, we will denote the characteristics and limitations of the method. We will follow this by covering optical imaging. As we go from fundamentals to systems and applications, and finally to challenges and outlook, discussion will be steered towards its features complementary to those of acoustic techniques. Finally, the last third section of the course will be on the study of photoacoustic (optoacoustic) methods, where we combine optical excitation and acoustic detection. 二、參考書籍 (References)- Biomedical Optics: Principles and Imaging by Hsin-I Wu and Lihong V. Wang- Photoacoustic Imaging and Spectroscopy by Lihong V. Wang- Journal articles (Photoacoustics, Nature Photonics, Light: Science & Applications, Theranostics...etc)- Supplementary handouts三、教學方式(Teaching Method)This course will be a combination of lectures and group discussions. Students will be encouraged to deduct and reason for the purpose of developing critical thinking as well as reinforce cognitive participation. Homework will be designed to challenge the students’ literature search ability, along with analytical and presentations skills.四、教學進度(Syllabus)Course outline1. Introduction: motivations, techniques, and challenges2. Image characterization: common features3. Ultrasound: intro and overview4. Ultrasound: acoustic wave propagation5. Ultrasound: transducers and image formation6. Ultrasound: systems and applications7. Optical Imaging: light propagation8. Optical Imaging: methods and applications9. Optical Imaging: summary10. Optoacoustics: fundamentals11. Optoacoustics: systems and applications12. Optoacoustics: challenges and outlook13. Summary五、成績考核(Evaluation)Class participation (30%)Assignment (40%)Exam (30%)---------------------------------------------生成式人工智慧倫理聲明 「有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出」基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用AI進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品質。根據本校公布之「大學教育場域AI協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取有條件開放，以下說明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式AI進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

course.description:
這門實習課程可於學期中或寒暑假期間進行。學生需在生物醫學工程相關公司完成至少 150小時的實務訓練。該課程旨在提
供生物醫學工程產
業的實務經驗，並將理論知識與專業實踐相結合。
This internship course may be undertaken during the academic semester or in the summer/winter break. 
Students are required to complete at least 150 hours of practical training at one or several 
biomedical 
engineering–related company. The program is designed to provide hands-on experience in the 
biomedical 
engineering industry and to bridge theoretical knowledge with professional practice.

It also strengthens workplace safety education and encourages students to explore professional fields and workplaces with an open mind while trying to build future career networks.(2)教學進度及方式(Teaching Schedule and Methods)(2.1) After attending the corporate internship orientation, students interested in participating must submit an application.(2.2) Students’ interests will be matched with internship projects offered by companies.(2.3) Internship hours: Students will complete at least 150 hours of internship according to a schedule during the semester or winter/summer breaks.(2.4) Oral presentation: Used to evaluate students’ internship performance.(2.5) Internship journal observation: Interns will have discussions with company mentors (senior R&D technical staff or HR), and the school may conduct occasional visits.(2.6) Final presentation: Within ten days after the internship, students must submit a project and internship report.(3)成績考核(Evaluation)(3.1) Grading criteria: based on a 100-point scale, with 70 or above as “Pass”.(3.2) Score breakdown: Internship report 40%, mentor evaluation 30%, midterm report 10%, attendance and attitude 10%, counseling and visit evaluation 10%.(3.3) Internship grades will be signed and evaluated by the company mentor and then submitted to the school for approval.(4)採用下列何項AI使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI)有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output本課程學生需在透明與負責任的原則下，適度使用AI工具進行課業協作。學生應在課堂作業或報告的標題頁註腳或引用文獻後，簡要說明如何使用生成式AI進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等內容。然而，在「個人反思報告」和「小組採訪作業」中，禁止使用生成式AI工具進行撰寫。如經查核未標註AI工具的使用情況，教師或學校有權重新評分或不予計分。Students in this course are expected to use AI tools appropriately for academic collaboration under the principles of transparency and accountability. course.description:
Net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 is necessary to limit the global temperature increase within 1.5 
C and avoid irreversible damage from global warming.  Fossil fuel power plants are responsible for 
the most carbon emissions among the anthropogenic sources.  Carbon capture and sequestration (CCS) 
is an essential technology to decarbonize power generation and achieve the net-zero carbon 
emission target.  This course will focus on the CCS technology development in the context of 
mitigating the global warming.  In this class, the students will be expected to learn:
1.	The greenhouse gas sources and the mitigation methods 
2.	The low-emission power generation technology 
3.	The carbon capture and sequestration technology with amine scrubbing
4.	Current status of carbon capture in industry

mechanical properties. This course is divided into three parts: (1) Microstructure of materials,

theory of vacancies and dislocations). (2) Thermodynamics and kinetics of materials Science: phase

microstructure of materials. (3) Properties of materials: discussing the physical, chemical, and 
mechanical properties of metals, ceramics, composite materials, and semiconductors.

course.description:
This course provides an introduction to polymer materials and processing technologies, with an 
emphasis on the relationship between polymer structure, material properties, and processing behavior. 
Topics include polymer classification, molecular structure, crystallinity, mechanical behavior, 
viscoelasticity, creep, stress relaxation, and melt flow characteristics. The course further 
introduces major polymer processing methods, including extrusion, injection molding, additive 
manufacturing, advanced packaging, and fiber-reinforced composite processing. Students will learn how 
processing conditions influence polymer flow, deformation, material structure, and final product 
performance. Applications of computer-aided engineering (CAE) in polymer processing and packaging will 
also be discussed.
course.objectives: Course keywords: 高分子材料, 高分子流變性質, 高分子機械性質，模具設計，電腦輔助工程分析, Injection molding, extrusion, polymer, fiber reinforced composites，塑膠加工, 先進封裝      一、課程說明(Course Description)本課程旨在提供學生對高分子材料與其加工技術的全面認識，內容涵蓋從材料基礎、機械行為、流變性質，到實際加工應用，包含在先進封裝技術的應用。課程前半段將介紹天然與合成高分子材料的基本聚合反應、熱塑性與熱固性塑膠、彈性體等分類，並深入探討聚合度、結晶度與無定形特性對材料性能的影響。此外，也將說明分子鏈結構與材料應用之間的關聯。接續將探討高分子材料的機械行為，包括其在應力與應變下展現的彈性、塑性與黏彈性特性，並進一步說明潛變、應力鬆弛與疲勞等時間相關的力學行為。接下來透過高分子熔體的流動行為學習溫度、剪切速率與分子量對流動性的影響，並認識黏彈性理論與基本流變測試儀器。課程後半著重於實務加工技術，包括擠出成型（單螺桿與雙螺桿）、射出成型與模具設計，並進一步介紹高分子混煉與共混、纖維強化複合材料等應用技術。在半導體封裝方面，將說明CoWoS、FOWLP等先進封裝技術對材料性能與製程的挑戰。此外，也將介紹電腦輔助工程（CAE）在高分子加工與封裝中的應用，以提升製程模擬與產品設計效率。本課程適合對高分子材料有興趣，並希望深入了解其於各項製程領域應用的學生，為未來從事材料開發、製程優化奠定扎實基礎。This course provides students with a comprehensive introduction to polymer materials and processing technologies. Topics include polymer classification, structure–property relationships, mechanical behavior, melt flow characteristics, and practical processing applications.The first part of the course introduces thermoplastics, thermosets, elastomers, and natural and synthetic polymers, with emphasis on how molecular structure, degree of polymerization, crystallinity, and amorphous characteristics influence material properties. The course also covers the mechanical behavior of polymers, including elasticity, plasticity, viscoelasticity, creep, and stress relaxation.The second part focuses on polymer processing technologies and applications, including extrusion, injection molding, additive manufacturing, advanced packaging, and fiber-reinforced composite processing. Students will learn how polymer melts flow, deform, and solidify during processing, and how processing conditions affect material structure and final properties. Applications of computer-aided engineering (CAE) in polymer processing and packaging will also be introduced.This course is suitable for students interested in polymer materials, materials processing, and engineering applications, and provides a foundation for further study in polymer processing, composite materials, process design, and materials development.二、指定用書(Text Books) 1. course.description:
本課程為包含化工系大學部必修課程兩部分之簡述:輸送現象與化工單元操作。課程目的在於提供化工所同學對化工

course.objectives: Course keywords: pump, flow meters, heat exchanger, dryer, distillation, leaching, extraction, absorption, adsorption, mechanical separation      一、	課程說明(Course Description) This course is designed to provide basic understanding of transport phenomena and unit operations for graduate students with a non-chemical engineering undergraduate background. It is divided into two parts. The first part takes 9 weeks to cover physical properties (viscosity, conductivity, diffusivity) and (momentum, energy, mass) transport mechanisms, and shell balance techniques for solving physical quantity (velocity, temperature, concentration) distributions in simple transport problems. The second part focuses on several key unit operations such as fluid delivery, mixing, separation and heating and drying that are critical for students to learn so that they can apply some basic knowledge and skill in this area when they start to work in domestic plants.二、指定用書(Text Books) Bird, R.B., W.E. Stewart, and E.N. Lightfoot, "Transport Phenomena," 2nd ed., Wiley (2002)三、參考書籍(References) 王茂齡, “輸送現象” 高立圖書 (1993)Middleman, S., “An Introduction to Fluid Mechanics” and “An Introduction to Mass and Heat Transfer”, Wiley(1998)四、教學方式(Teaching Method) lectures五、教學進度(Syllabus) Transport phenomena: 3 weeks for momentum transport, 3 weeks for energy transport, and 3 weeks for mass transportUnit operations: Fluid delivery (2 weeks), mixing(2 weeks), separation (2 weeks), heating and drying(2 weeks).六、成績考核(Evaluation) Transport Phenomena:1 Midterm Examination 45% Weekly in-class practice 10%Unit operations:1. Final Examination 25%2. Project & presentation 20%● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI):本課程無涉及AI使用 Not applicable七、可連結之網頁位址

course.titleEn: Principles and Applications of Small Angle Scattering
course.requirement: 化工系115D 選修 化工系115M 選修
course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
This course will cover the principles and applications of small angle X-ray and neutron scattering, 
which are important tools for exploring the nanostructures, thermodynamics and dynamics of matters.  
The objective is to provide the students a solid background on these techniques, which may be 
helpful for their research in related subjects.  The topics covered in this course are outlined as 
follows. 

1. Basics of X-ray and Neutron Scattering
2. Small Angle Scattering
2. Applications to Polymer Blends and Block Copolymers
4. Application to Amorphous Polymers
5. Study of Surfaces and Interfaces
6. Inelastic Scattering for Dynamics Studies

The materials taught in class will be based largely on the book of:  
R. J. Roe, “Methods of X-ray and Neutron Scattering in Polymer Science”, Oxford University Press 
(2000)

Two exams will be held and a final written report is required.

course.description:
This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical and 
practical aspects of computational modeling in chemical and materials systems. Through this course, 
students will develop proficiency in computational thinking, which involves the analysis of 
characteristic scales (time and length) relevant to the problems of interest, and the utilization of 
associated computational tools.
course.objectives: Course keywords: 電腦模擬、原子尺度模擬、第一原理計算、分子動力學模擬      一、課程說明(Course Description)This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical and practical aspects of computational modeling in chemical and materials systems. Through this course, students will develop proficiency in computational thinking, which involves the analysis of characteristic scales (time and length) relevant to the problems of interest, and the utilization of associated computational tools.This course is designed for students in chemical engineering. Therefore, the course emphasizes a hands-on approach where students are requested to investigate three classic types of systems in chemical engineering via computational approaches:1. Organic semiconductors (ab-initio gas-phase computations: MO, IE/EA, vibrational spectroscopy, thermodynamic properties (harmonic approximation), excited-state properties)2. Surface catalytic reactions (ab-initio solid-state simulations: band structure, work function, adsorption energy, volcano plot, activation energy barrier)3. Predictions of thermodynamic properties (classical force-field molecular dynamics simulations: vapor-liquid equilibrium, activity coefficient)Overall, the course is designed to equip students with the necessary skills and knowledge to apply computational techniques to real-world problems in the field of chemical and materials systems.This course is a bit demanding, and it is strongly recommended that the students know some basic knowledge of:1. Quantum chemistry/ quantum mechanics2. Python3. Thermodynamics and statistical thermodynamics4. Solid-state physicsThis course places a strong emphasis on pre-reading assigned materials and in-class discussions. This component will account for 25% of the total grade.二、指定用書(Text Books)No三、參考書籍(References)Quantum chemistry and quantum mechanics:1. Molecular Quantum Mechanics / Peter Atkins2. Introduction to Quantum Mechanics / David J. GriffithsComputational chemistry:1. Essentials of Computational Chemistry: Theories and Models / Christopher J. Cramer2. Introduction to Computational Chemistry / Frank JensenMaterials modeling1. Introduction to Computational Materials Science: Fundamentals to Applications / Richard LeSar2. Materials Modelling Using Density Functional Theory: Properties and Predictions / Feliciano GiustinoDensity functional theory(DFT/TD-DFT)1. A Chemist's Guide to Density Functional Theory / Koch and Max C. Holthausen2. Time-Dependent Density-Functional Theory: Concepts and Applications / Carsten A. UllrichMolecular dynamics simulations (MD)1. Understanding Molecular Simulation: From Algorithms to Applications / Berend Smit and Daan Frenkel2. Computer Simulation of Liquids / D. J. Tildesley and M.P. Allen四、教學方式(Teaching Method)Lectures (2 courses) + hands-on session (1+ course)五、教學進度(Syllabus)1. (5 weeks) Organic semiconductors (ab-initio gas-phase computations: MO, IE/EA, vibrational spectroscopy, thermodynamic properties (harmonic approximation), excited-state properties)2. (4 weeks) Surface catalytic reactions (ab-initio solid-state simulations: band structure, work function, adsorption energy, volcano plot, activation energy barrier)3. (4 weeks) Predictions of thermodynamic properties (classical force-field molecular dynamics simulations: vapor-liquid equilibrium, activity coefficient)4. (3 weeks) Final presentation六、成績考核(Evaluation)Quiz and in-class performance 15%4 Homework sets 60% Final Presentation 25%七、可連結之網頁位址No八、AI使用規則1. 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。2. 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

course.description:
本課程是有機化學專業實作科目，基於實作安全及難度考量，修習前須經過普化實驗之基礎訓練。本課程將連結實驗、儀器
及生活應用，目的在訓練學生獨立思考完成實作，將實驗結果利用儀器進行分析並和生活應用連結。 
1.選擇新奇有趣及生活化的教材：使用原文教學實驗課本，加強學生閱讀外語文章及熟悉化學專業用語。選新奇有趣及生活 
化的實驗(如從天然物裡取得有用的純化物、生化藥物抗生素之全合成、化學鑑定所使用魯米諾的合成及放光等)，激發學生
做實驗的興趣並能更有切身的體會。 
2.嚴謹扎實的實驗訓練及經驗的傳承：有機實驗基本技巧是所有實驗的根本，加強訓練基礎技巧。督促學生邊實驗邊思考問 
題及預判可能發展性，才能養成其從事研究之獨立思考能力。加強實作經驗的傳承，連想思考研究方向及知道如何開始著手 
解決問題。
3.藥品安全與增添特殊器材增廣見識：養成學生閱讀藥品性質的習慣，隨時閱讀該藥品性質及知悉其危險性，增加使用藥品 
安全性。增添新器材的使用，如短管蒸餾、冷凝管、乾浴器等應用等，讓實驗更多元化更活用器材的運用度。

course.description:

中各項主題，並著眼在基本知識的學習和思考能力的啟發，以作為未來深入研究的基石。

course.objectives: Course keywords: 有機化學 organic chemistry, 無機化學 inorganic chemistry, 批判性思考 critical thinking, 學術口頭表達 academic oral presentation, 文獻探討 literature review      課程說明 (Course Description)本課程旨在透過化學專業情境培養學生之學術英語能力，並聚焦於有機化學與無機化學之最新研究發展。學生將學習如何搜尋、閱讀、評估與整理近期學術文獻，掌握當前研究趨勢與前沿議題。透過口頭報告、結構化討論及文獻探討，學生將訓練以英語清楚且專業地表達科學概念。課程亦強調批判性思考、證據導向論述、科學推理，以及學術討論中的即時應答能力，同時鼓勵跨領域連結與研究興趣探索，作為未來學術發展之基礎。本課程採三人小組合作模式，每次由一位學生進行專題口頭報告，一位學生擔任主持人引導討論，另一位學生負責整理問題與討論紀錄。其餘學生亦以三人小組方式參與，每場報告後進行 5 分鐘討論，並提出至少一個問題作為全班討論基礎。教學方式 (Teaching Methods)1. 口頭報告每位學生須選擇一篇與有機化學或無機化學相關之期刊論文，經授課教師核准後進行報告。論文選擇條件：期刊 Impact Factor > 4發表年份：2024–2026同儕審查之研究型論文口頭報告14天前，需準備3–5頁投影片，與老師討論報告內容與架構。口頭報告要求：報告時間 25 分鐘開場重點摘要 3–5 分鐘含問答討論時間2. 課程進行方式本課程採分組專題討論方式進行。學生以三人為一組，每次報告由一組負責，其中一人擔任口頭報告者，進行 25 分鐘專題文獻報告；一人擔任主持人，負責介紹主題、掌握時間、引導討論與協助問答進行；另一人擔任問題整理者，負責記錄各組提問、現場討論內容與課後彙整。每場報告結束後，其餘同學亦以三人為一組進行 5 分鐘小組討論。各組需根據報告內容提出至少一個問題，問題可包含文獻理解、研究方法、數據詮釋、實驗設計、研究限制或未來延伸等面向。各組提出之問題將作為課堂討論基礎，並納入課程參與評量。本課程強調學生不僅需具備文獻閱讀與口頭表達能力，也需學習主持學術討論、提出具批判性之問題，並透過同儕互動深化對研究內容的理解。透過報告、主持、提問與討論紀錄等不同角色，學生將培養科學溝通、批判思考與團隊合作能力。3. 文獻探討與摘要寫作學生須於報告前一週繳交所選論文與摘要，供教師與同學預先閱讀。4. 教師與同儕回饋報告與討論表現將由教師與同儕共同評分，重視學術內容深度、表達能力與專業態度。成績考核 (Evaluation)1. 簡報表現 (Presentation Skills)：50%2. 口頭表達與儀態 (Delivery & Professionalism)：10%3. 問答表現 (Answers to Questions)：10%4. 提問與參與討論 (Question Raising & Participation)：10%5. 文獻選擇與摘要品質 (Paper Selection & Abstract Quality)：5%6. 出席率與準時性 (Attendance & Punctuality)：5%7. 同儕評分 (Peer Evaluation)：10%AI 使用規則 (Select Applicable AI Usage Policy Policy)有條件開放，學生可使用生成式 AI 協助下列事項：文法修正與語言潤飾；專業詞彙提升；簡報架構發想；背景知識整理；發音與口語練習輔助。學生須於簡報中明確註明 AI 使用方式與範圍。學生不得使用 AI 進行以下行為：捏造數據、文獻或研究結果；錯誤詮釋論文內容；取代本人閱讀原始論文；未經實質修改即直接提交 AI 生成內容。所有作業之正確性、原創性與學術誠信，仍由學生本人負責。

Students will give oral presentations in English and actively participate in class discussions.指定用書 (Text Books)無指定教科書。No designated textbook.參考書籍 (References)以近五年內發表於 SCI/SCIE 收錄期刊，且與分析化學相關之原始研究論文為主。所選論文須具有明確的分析化學內容或方法上的創新性，不接受發表於掠奪性期刊（predatory journals）之論文。所有報告文獻須經授課教師確認。Recent original research articles published within the past five years in reputable SCI/SCIE-indexed journals related to analytical chemistry. Articles published in predatory journals will not be accepted. All selected articles must be approved by the instructor.教學方式 (Teaching Methods)課程包括教師講授、文獻研讀、學生口頭報告及課堂討論。學生須閱讀並理解所選論文，以英文進行科學簡報，並回答教師及同學的問題。Lectures, literature study, student presentations, and class discussion. Students are expected to understand the selected articles, present them clearly in English, and participate actively in discussion.教學進度 (Course Schedule)Week 1 — Course Introduction課程介紹、評分方式、文獻選擇原則及報告要求。Week 2 — Literature Search and Article Selection如何搜尋、篩選及評估適合書報討論的分析化學文獻。Week 3 — How to Give a Scientific Presentation科學簡報的架構、研究背景與研究問題的介紹、結果呈現、科學論述及問答技巧。Week 4 — Effective PowerPoint for Scientific Presentations科學簡報投影片的製作，包括版面、文字、圖表、資訊呈現及常見問題。Week 5 onward — Student Presentations and Discussion學生依排定順序進行報告。每次報告後進行問答、討論及回饋。The detailed presentation schedule will be adjusted according to class size and course progress.成績考核 (Evaluation)Literature search and article selection: 15%Scientific presentation and slide quality: 30%Understanding and critical evaluation of the literature: 30%Questions and answers: 15%Class participation and discussion: 10%請假依《國立清華大學學生請假辦法》辦理。若因請假無法進行原訂報告，請事先通知授課教師，並另行安排補報告。Absence and leave will follow the NTHU Student Leave Regulations. Students who are unable to give a scheduled presentation should notify the instructor in advance and arrange a make-up presentation.AI 使用規則 (AI Usage Policy)有條件開放使用 (Conditionally open)可使用生成式 AI 協助英文文法修正、文字潤飾及簡報架構整理，但不得取代學生本人對原始論文的閱讀、理解及批判性分析。學生須自行確認所有科學內容及引用資料的正確性，並對報告內容負責。Generative AI may be used for language editing and organization of presentation materials, but it should not replace the student's own reading, understanding, and critical evaluation of the original literature. Students are responsible for the accuracy of all scientific content and references.與課程相關的網站 (Course-related Website)NTHU eeclasshttps://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

We can understand the reaction mechanism, the synthetic technology and understand a variety of cyclization reactions and asymmetric stereochemistry via the applications of organometallic synthesis with main group elements.Organometallic chemistry, course planning is as follows:(1) Introduction of Organometallic Chemistry(a) Organometallic structures, energy levels of d-orbital, electron counting and the 18 electron rule(b) Discussion of metal-ligand bonding: alkyne, olefin, carbon monoxide, methylene, benzene and cyclopentadiene(c) Mechanism and theory of organometallics: oxidative addition, reductive elimination and migration & insertion reactions.(d) Electrophilic & nucleophilic reaction and carbon-carbon bond formation.(2) Organometallics in organic synthesis.(a)Organometallic synthesis and applications with main group and halogen.(b) Organometallic synthesis with σ bond and Cu, Zn, Cr(c) Transition metals in catalytic coupling reaction(d) Catalytic reaction of σ bond. (e) Catalytic reaction of π system: alkyne, propenyl and ethynyl group(f) Cyclization reaction and asymmetric stereochemistry(g) Asymmetric catalytic reaction

course.description:
The organic Synthesis I course will cover enolate chemistry with C-C bond formations through 
alkylation and additions to aldehydes and 
ketones as well as nucleophilic acyl substitution. Some functional group interversions through 
substitution chemistry will be discussed. 
Due to functional group compatibility issues, suitable functional group protections and subsequent 
deprotections are required. 
Electrophilic additions to C=C and CC triple bonds will be discussed along with stereo- selectivity 
issues. Diels-Alder type 
cycloadditions, rearrangement chemistry and thermal elimination will be covered. Final discussion of 
pericyclic reaction will be centered 
on electrocyclization.

course.description:

擇近期發表之高品質分析化學研究論文，整理研究背景、分析方法、主要結果及研究的重要性，並於課堂中進行口頭報告與討論。

The purpose of this seminar course is to develop essential skills for graduate research in analytical chemistry. Students will learn to 
critically read and evaluate recent scientific literature, organize scientific information, give oral presentations in English, answer 
questions, and participate actively in scientific discussions.
course.objectives: Course keywords: Analytical Chemistry, Literature Search, Scientific Presentation, Scientific Discussion, Critical Thinking      課程說明 (Course Description)本課程旨在訓練學生閱讀與分析近期分析化學文獻，並培養科學簡報、批判性思考及學術討論能力。學生將選擇近期研究論文，以英文進行口頭報告，並參與課堂問答與討論。This course aims to develop students’ skills in reading and critically evaluating recent literature in analytical chemistry, as well as scientific presentation and discussion. Students will give oral presentations in English and actively participate in class discussions.指定用書 (Text Books)無指定教科書。No designated textbook.參考書籍 (References)以近五年內發表於 SCI/SCIE 收錄期刊，且與分析化學相關之原始研究論文為主。所選論文須具有明確的分析化學內容或方法上的創新性，不接受發表於掠奪性期刊（predatory journals）之論文。所有報告文獻須經授課教師確認。Recent original research articles published within the past five years in reputable SCI/SCIE-indexed journals related to analytical chemistry. Articles published in predatory journals will not be accepted. All selected articles must be approved by the instructor.教學方式 (Teaching Methods)課程包括教師講授、文獻研讀、學生口頭報告及課堂討論。學生須閱讀並理解所選論文，以英文進行科學簡報，並回答教師及同學的問題。Lectures, literature study, student presentations, and class discussion. Students are expected to understand the selected articles, present them clearly in English, and participate actively in discussion.教學進度 (Course Schedule)Week 1 — Course Introduction課程介紹、評分方式、文獻選擇原則及報告要求。Week 2 — Literature Search and Article Selection如何搜尋、篩選及評估適合書報討論的分析化學文獻。Week 3 — How to Give a Scientific Presentation科學簡報的架構、研究背景與研究問題的介紹、結果呈現、科學論述及問答技巧。Week 4 — Effective PowerPoint for Scientific Presentations科學簡報投影片的製作，包括版面、文字、圖表、資訊呈現及常見問題。Week 5 onward — Student Presentations and Discussion學生依排定順序進行報告。每次報告後進行問答、討論及回饋。The detailed presentation schedule will be adjusted according to class size and course progress.成績考核 (Evaluation)Literature search and article selection: 15%Scientific presentation and slide quality: 30%Understanding and critical evaluation of the literature: 30%Questions and answers: 15%Class participation and discussion: 10%請假依《國立清華大學學生請假辦法》辦理。若因請假無法進行原訂報告，請事先通知授課教師，並另行安排補報告。Absence and leave will follow the NTHU Student Leave Regulations. Students who are unable to give a scheduled presentation should notify the instructor in advance and arrange a make-up presentation.AI 使用規則 (AI Usage Policy)有條件開放使用 (Conditionally open)可使用生成式 AI 協助英文文法修正、文字潤飾及簡報架構整理，但不得取代學生本人對原始論文的閱讀、理解及批判性分析。學生須自行確認所有科學內容及引用資料的正確性，並對報告內容負責。Generative AI may be used for language editing and organization of presentation materials, but it should not replace the student's own reading, understanding, and critical evaluation of the original literature. Students are responsible for the accuracy of all scientific content and references.與課程相關的網站 (Course-related Website)NTHU eeclasshttps://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

course.description:
本課程專為從未學過華語之學生所設計，從發音及拼音開始教授，讓學生在短時間內學會一些常用的基本日常生活用語，內容主題涵蓋：
簡單的自我介紹、打招呼、談論家人、愛好、購物、食物、地點、方位及時間，並能用中文詢問及回應選擇性問題進而給予簡單建議。
Mandarin Basic I is designed for students who have not previously studied Chinese. The course covers 
the phonetic system (Hanyu Pinyin), tones, grammar, writing, and daily conversation. The content 
includes self-introduction, greetings, family, hobbies, shopping, food, location, and time. 
Additionally, students will learn how to ask and answer simple questions, as well as make simple 
suggestions. The curriculum includes listening, speaking, reading and writing.

course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
1.本課程除了希望學生對於簡短的言談，能理解內容與掌握重點、能使用簡單的短語或句子敘述解釋原因或說明理由、
日常生活中熟悉的事物及每日例行性事務，並能簡單地描述事件及短片的內容。
2.內容涵蓋：旅遊計劃／交通工具、休閒活動、食物、租屋、
未來計畫及個人經驗、電話用語、表達祝賀與祝福、天氣、比較兩個事件、身體症狀等。

course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
1.	本課程希望學生能以中文表達比較、妥協及建議，並能用中文描述日常生活時程及學習語言的經驗與過去的 學、經歷
背景；此外，能使用中文提出假設性問題或回應該類問題；就文化部分，除了讓學生了解台灣婚禮傳統並能表達對文化差異之體
認及對新事物的看法。
This course focuses on using comparisons, compromises and suggestions in Chinese, and be able to use 
Chinese to describe daily life schedules and language learning experiences; in addition, students 
should be able to use Chinese to ask hypothetical questions or respond to them. For the cultural part, 
allowing students to understand Taiwan’s wedding traditions and express their understanding of 
cultural differences.
2.	內容涵蓋：問路、交通方式、專業領域相關詞語、祝賀語、
租屋、喜好等。The content including asking for directions, transportation methods,words related to 
professional fields, congratulations, renting a house,
preferences, etc.

course.description:
本課程為國語/華語為第一語言的台灣、海外華人社會或中國大陸的學生修讀。本課程旨在以輕鬆的學習模式，透過不同的情
境訓練學生廣東話的口頭表達能力及聽力理解。課堂活動以學生及語言技能主導並根據日常用語及基礎詞彙設計，內容側重
聽、講技能。

本課程提供多次實務練習，讓學生學習及應用基本廣東話，以應付課堂及工作上的需要。

The course is designed for Putonghua-speaking students from Taiwan, overseas Chinese Societies or 
Mainland China, who are looking for survival skills in Cantonese. The course is structured to help 
students communicate orally with the local people of Hong Kong in Cantonese in different scenarios, 
with student-centred, proficiency-orientated activities based on useful daily expressions and 
basic 
vocabulary items. The course focuses on student’s oral skills and speaking ability.

This course provides multiple practical exercises for students. It assists students to learn and 
apply Cantonese in their lessons or at work.

course.description:
1.本課程著重在短期內讓學生有中文基本會話能力，可以應付日常生活的需要。課程內容包括拼音、自我介紹、數字、購
物、時間、顏色、服裝、打電話等。
The Basic Conversation I is a course that helps students to build up their basic communication 
skills in Chinese within a short period of time, so they can deal with problems that might occur in 
daily life. The course will be covering basic phonics, selfintroduction, numbers, shopping, paying 
for things, telling time, colors, clothes, making phone calls, etc.
2. 建議同時修習《初級華語一》。
Highly recommend to take this course in tandem with along with Mandarin Basic I.

course.description:
1. 本課程希望能協助學習者發展其基礎級之聽說能力，透過日常生活會話與交際，協助其熟悉生活化且自然的表達方

This course aims to help learners develop basic-level listening and speaking abilities through 
everyday conversations and communicative interactions, enabling them to become familiar with natural 
and practical expressions used in daily life. 
2. 內容涵蓋華語學習者在台生活情境中常遇到的情境，如：聊天氣、景點、旅行、面試準備、約時間、問路、請求協
助等等。 
The course content covers common situations that Chinese language learners may encounter while 
living in Taiwan, such as talking about the weather, discussing tourist attractions and 
travel, preparing for interviews, making appointments, asking for directions, and requesting 
assistance.

This course aims to develop intermediate-level listening and
speaking skills, focusing on everyday expressions and
communicative patterns to enhance natural, fluent oral
expression and performance in oral presentations.
2. 涵蓋五大主題範疇：人際關係、節慶假日、防災準備、
時事議題，以及人文與信仰等。
The course covers five major thematic areas: interpersonal
relationships, festivals and holidays, disaster preparedness,
current events, and culture and beliefs.

course.description:
1.	本課程除了加強口語訓練之外，並開始由長篇對話進入書面語及篇章的訓練。
Besides strengthening oral training, this course also begins with long conversations to enter formal 
language and discourse training.
2.	內容主題涵蓋學校生活、購物、氣候、節日、社會環境、流行文化、台灣農業等。
The content topics include school life, shopping, weather, holidays, social environment, popular 
culture, and Taiwan agriculture, among others.
3.	學生可以學到詳述學習經驗、說服他人、了解簡單的規章合約、表達抗議、描述氣侯與傳統節日、如何強調、舉例、
提供進一步訊息、以不同意見反駁他人觀點、解釋選擇事物的理由等。
Students can learn to describe learning experiences, persuade others, understand simple rules and 
contracts, express protests, describe weather and traditional holidays, emphasize points, provide 
examples, offer further information, counter others' viewpoints with different opinions, and explain 
reasons for choosing things, and more.

course.description:
本課程以長篇對話及篇章兩種形式，擴展能談論的話題。內容主題涵蓋網路、藝術活動、科技、風水、經濟情況、地震等。 
學生能討論現實與虛擬的不同、介紹自己喜歡的藝術活動、討論科技正面與負面的影響、討論風水與迷信的關係與不同、表達出
所觀察到的社會轉變、談論災害發生的原因及地區等。

course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
1.本課程以長篇對話及章兩種形式，擴展能談論的話題。

2.內容主題涵蓋大學生活、社會現象歷史就業結構的改變、政治等。

3.學生能談論大與未來的活規劃、傳統觀念現代不同歷史事件的影響與改變、個人學經；了解台灣社會族群和語言文化的多
元；對政治提出自己看法，表達個人意見並說服他等。

course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
1.	本課程主要為閱讀篇章，從而擴展談論的話題。
This course primarily focuses on reading passages to expand the range of topics for discussion.
2.	內容主題涵蓋自由、民生、社會現象等層面。
The content themes cover aspects such as freedom, livelihood, social phenomena, etc.
3.	學生能談論言論與自由的關係、食品安全、外貌與內在、時代及思想轉變等議題。
Students are able to discuss topics such as the relationship between speech and freedom, food safety, 
appearance versus inner qualities, changes in eras and ideologies, etc.

course.description:
本課程為針對母語非華語的國際學生所設計，選材自真實語篇。涵蓋國際社會多面向的新聞主題及議題。
This course is designed for international students whose native language is not Chinese, with 
materials selected from authentic texts. It covers a wide range of news topics and issues in the 
international community.

course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
本課程的學習對象以華語文能力測驗（TOCFL）B1以上學生為宜。教學方式與預期目標為：
1 透過探討重大且具爭議的公共議題，提升學生以華語表達立場與評論的能力。
2.利用「問題解決導向」的學習模式引導學生有效率地達到上述1的語文能力。
3.要求學生切實完成單元主題作業練習，教師糾錯以降低學生系統性語用偏誤。

course.syllabusSource: 清大官方課程系統大綱（由 NTHUMods 公開索引整理）
course.description:
本課程為針對母語非華語的國際學生所設計，選材自真實語篇。涵蓋社會、科技、經濟、政治、文化、環境等多元主題，拓展學生對不同
語體、領域的語言認知與運用。上完課後，華語程度約可達到 CEFR C1 (ACTFL Superior) 的程度。本課程適合學習時數超過700小
時，具備4000個詞彙量的學習者。
This course is designed for international students whose native language is not Chinese. It uses 
authentic language materials covering diverse topics such as society, technology, economics, 
politics, culture, and the environment. It aims to expand students' language awareness and usage 
across different registers and domains. After completing the course, students' Chinese proficiency 
level is expected to reach approximately CEFR C1 (ACTFL Superior). This course is suitable for 
learners who have studied for over 700 hours and have a vocabulary of 4000 words.

展學生對不同語體、領域的語言認知與運用。上完課後，華語程度約可達到 CEFR C1 (ACTFL Superior) 的程度。本課程
適合學習時數超過750小時，具備4500個詞彙量的學習者。 
This course is designed for international students whose native language is not Chinese. It uses 
authentic language materials covering diverse topics such as society, technology, economics, 
politics, culture, and the environment. It aims to expand students' language awareness and usage 
across different registers and domains. After completing the course, students' Chinese 
proficiency level is expected to reach approximately CEFR C1 (ACTFL Superior). This course is 
suitable for learners who have studied for over 750 hours and have a vocabulary of 4500 words.

course.description:
本課程目標為幫助國際學生學習及體驗職場或商業情境的中文，內容包含如何找工作、面試、應聘、上班族日常開會、出差
及辦公環境、商務表單填寫等。為了配合大多正式的商務情境需要，課程除了口語的練習之外，亦涵蓋書面語的應用文書練
習，如開會通知、議程、公告文書等。進度預定為每兩週一課。
This course is designed to assist international students learn and experience Mandarin in workplace 
or business contexts. The course content includes topics such as job searching, interviews, 
employment procedures, office meetings, business trips, work environments, and completing business 
sheets/forms. 
In addition to spoken language practice, the course also covers formal written skills to meet the 
demands of more formal business situations, such as meeting notices, agendas, and official 
announcements. The course is structured to cover one lesson every two weeks.

course.description:
This course covers the fundamental theories of digital communication systems. The
focus will be on the mathematical modeling of the communication systems and the
analysis of the system performance. The core concepts are: Signal Representation;
Spectral Analysis; Optimal Receiver for Coherent and Non-Coherent systems;
Probability of Error Analysis; Introduction to Information Theory; Bandlimited
Channels; InterSymbol Interference (ISI), Equalizers, Channel Capacity,
Multicarrier OFDM.

course.description:
This course teaches the fundamentals of multi-antenna communication, which is one of the key 
technologies in future wireless communication systems. Particularly, the use of antenna array 
deliveries substantial improvements to wireless system performance in terms of data rate, number of 
connected devices, and power efficiency. This course aims to provide students with a solid 
understanding of multi-antenna communications including system modeling, channel capacity theories, 
and transceiver design.

course.description:

5G/6G NTN。這些技術在全球行動通訊、物聯網 (IoT) 以及寬頻互聯網服務中扮演重要角色。本課程旨在提供通訊相關領域的
學生完整的衛星通訊知識，使其具備理解、設計及應用現代衛星通訊系統的能力。

Digital Communication System Principles（數位通訊系統原理）2.	Digital Modulation and Multiple Access Techniques（數位調變與多重存取技術）3.	Introduction to Satellite Orbits（衛星軌道簡介）4. course.description:
This course introduces what is System-on-Chip (SoC),  benefits of using SoC,  system architecture, 
design methodology and its applications. It uses several SoC designs, such as computer chip sets, 
cell phone IC, multimedia ICs, wireless communication ICs,  information appliances and interface 
ICs, as examples to illustrate the top-down IC design flow, Intellectual Property(IP), system 
platform design and their market applications. The computer chip sets covers personal computer 
architectures, memory and peripheral I/O interface chip design. The cell phone IC covers 
heterogeneous multi-processor (HMP). The wireless communication includes CDMA, OFDM and LTE, 4G and 
5G chip designs. The multimedia ICs covers audio, still image, and video, AR/VR ICs. The biomedical 
ICs covers Gene chip, Lab on a chip, and Ink-jet microarray. Emerging applications related SoC 
include autonomous vehicles, high resolution display, Internet of Things (IoT), 3D sensing, and deep 
learning acc

course.objectives: Course keywords: 永續科技Sustainable technology, 淨零轉型Net-zero transition, 循環經濟Circular economy, 生命週期評估Life cycle assessment, 能源轉型Energy transition, 資源循環Resource recovery, 系統思維 Systems thinking, ESG與治理ESG and governance      Detailed Course Syllabus● 課程說明(Course Description)本課程以「永續挑戰—科技回應—系統評估—實務提案」為主軸，協助研究生建立永續科技的共同語言與跨域分析能力。內容兼顧全球永續議題、淨零與碳管理、能源與材料轉型、循環經濟、資源與生物質利用、ESG治理與技術實作案例，並導入系統思維、生命週期觀點與利害關係人分析。課程特別強調將工程、科學、管理與政策串接，培養學生在研究、產業與公共治理場域中界定問題、評估方案與提出可行永續技術路徑之能力。● 指定用書(Text Books)1. 無單一指定教科書；以教師自編講義、案例教材及每週指定閱讀為主。2. 選讀書目將涵蓋永續工程、循環經濟、生命週期評估、淨零轉型與ESG相關主題。● 參考書籍(References)1. Mihelcic, J. R. & Zimmerman, J. B. Environmental Engineering: Fundamentals, Sustainability, Design.2. Ashby, M. Materials and the Environment: Eco-informed Material Choice.3. Ellen MacArthur Foundation 之循環經濟報告與案例資料。4. IPCC、IEA、UN SDGs、World Bank、OECD等國際組織之公開報告。5. 課堂另搭配近期國際期刊論文與本地產業/政策案例。● 教學方式(Teaching Method)課程採講授、案例研討、文獻導讀、分組討論、課堂工作坊、學生口頭報告及期末專題等方式進行。為強化研究所層級之實作能力，學生須以小組方式針對一項真實永續議題提出技術或系統改善方案，內容需包括問題定義、現況分析、技術選項比較、潛在效益與限制、以及實施建議。● 教學進度(Syllabus)週次	單元主題	主要活動 / 作業第1週	課程導論：何謂永續科技？學程定位、學習目標與評量方式	課程說明；分組；主題探索第2週	永續發展核心架構：SDGs、行星界限、三重底線與公正轉型	指定閱讀討論 1第3週	系統思維與永續問題界定：nexus、邊界設定、利害關係人分析	個人反思短文 1第4週	氣候變遷、碳管理與淨零路徑：碳盤查、MRV、減量與移除	案例分析 1第5週	能源轉型與低碳技術：再生能源、儲能、氫能與工業減排	課堂討論第6週	循環經濟與資源循環：廢棄物資源化、工業共生、產品服務系統	分組題目確立第7週	永續材料與綠色製程：材料選擇、低碳製造、替代原料	主題摘要提交第8週	生命週期思維：LCA、TEA、環境足跡與技術比較	案例分析 2第9週	永續生物技術與生物精煉案例：食品、生質能、資源化技術	期中專題構想報告第10週	水–能源–糧食–材料 nexus 與都市/產業永續	指定閱讀討論 2第11週	數位科技與永續：AI、資料治理、智慧監測與決策支援	個人反思短文 2第12週	ESG、永續金融與政策治理：揭露、法規、企業實務	案例分析 3第13週	技術導入與擴散：商業模式、社會接受度、風險與尺度化	專題進度檢核第14週	國內外校園、城市與產業案例整合工作坊	分組工作坊第15週	期末分組專題口頭報告 I	口頭報告與同儕回饋第16週	期末分組專題口頭報告II與課程總結	繳交期末書面報告● 成績考核(Evaluation)1. 課堂參與、出席及討論表現：15%2. 個人反思短文與指定閱讀回應：15%3. 個案分析作業（3次）：20%4. 期中分組專題構想報告：15%5. 期末分組專題書面報告：20%6. 期末分組口頭報告與同儕回饋：15%本課程以專題實作、案例分析與口頭報告為主要評量方式，不另設傳統筆試；評分重點在於問題界定能力、跨域整合、資料與論證品質、技術可行性分析，以及表達與回應能力。AI 使用規則 / AI Use Policy■ 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出生成式AI可用於主題發想、資料整理、語言潤飾、簡報架構設計與基礎視覺化輔助；但學生必須於作業或報告附錄中揭露使用之工具、用途與驗證方式，並對所有內容之正確性、引用與判讀負完全責任。禁止使用AI捏造數據、文獻、案例、圖表或訪談內容；未經查證直接提交AI生成內容，視同學術倫理違規。● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)學程網站：https://stmp.site.nthu.edu.tw/；課程資料另公告於校內教學平台。
